question: Shivam got an increase of 4% in his sales amount in the first year and 25% in the second year; also with this, his current sales are ₹1,40,400, what was his sales (in ₹) two years ago?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage increase = 4 + 25 + (4 × 25)/100 = 30%.

This means the current sales are 130% of the initial sales.

Initial sales = Current sales × (100 ÷ 130)

Initial sales = 140400 × (10 ÷ 13) = 108000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,08,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Current sales = ₹1,40,400

First year increase = 4%

Second year increase = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 + R₁/100) × (1 + R₂/100)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the sales two years ago be x.

⇒ x × (1 + 4/100) × (1 + 25/100) = 1,40,400

⇒ x × (104/100) × (125/100) = 1,40,400

⇒ x × (26/25) × (5/4) = 1,40,400

⇒ x × (130/100) = 1,40,400

⇒ x × 1.3 = 1,40,400

⇒ x = 1,40,400 ÷ 1.3

⇒ x = 1,08,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,08,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is increased successively by a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by the formula: Net Change = a + b + (a × b)/100.

Multiplier Method

To increase a number by r%, multiply it directly by its multiplier (1 + r/100). For successive changes across multiple periods, simply multiply all factors sequentially.

Reversing a Percentage Increase

If the final value is known after a total r% increase, the initial value can be found by multiplying the final value by 100 ÷ (100 + r).
